speaker: Doctor
text: I need to ask a few more questions to narrow this down. Have you noticed any recent changes in your bowel habits or stool color? Also, have you had any recent travel or exposure to tuberculosis?

speaker: Patient
text: I have been feeling very tired and have had worsening abdominal pain for about four weeks. I have also had drenching night sweats and lost about twelve pounds.

speaker: Doctor
text:
That weight loss is significant and concerning given your symptoms. Have you noticed any blood in your stool or stool that looks like tar? Also, do you have a history of smoking or a family history of lymphoma or gastrointestinal cancer?

REQUEST TEST: CBC with differential, Comprehensive Metabolic Panel, and LDH.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Complete Blood Count (WBC: Elevated, Hemoglobin: Slightly Decreased, Platelets: Normal), Comprehensive Metabolic Panel: NORMAL READINGS, Lactate Dehydrogenase (Elevated)

speaker: Patient
text: I noticed swelling in my neck over the last few days. It does not hurt, but it feels enlarged and fixed.

speaker: Patient
text: I also feel fullness in my abdomen and my clothes feel tighter. I do not have cough or recent travel.

speaker: Patient
text: I have smoked about one pack a day for many years, and I drink socially. The abdominal discomfort and fatigue have both been getting worse. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Tuberculosis and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the significant weight loss, night sweats, smoking history, and the specific location of your enlarged supraclavicular lymph node, we need to rule out malignancy despite the previous suggestion of tuberculosis. REQUEST TEST: LDH (Lactate Dehydrogenase) and ESR (Erythrocyte Sedimentation Rate). REQUEST IMAGES: CT Abdomen and Pelvis with contrast, and CT Chest.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: LDH: Elevated, ESR: NORMAL READINGS, CT Chest: Massively enlarged axillary, mediastinal, and cervical lymph nodes, CT Abdomen and Pelvis: Splenomegaly detected, dullness noted over the left lower quadrant, slight abdominal distension

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Hodgkin Lymphoma. The combination of B-symptoms (fever, night sweats, weight loss), supraclavicular lymphadenopathy, massively enlarged mediastinal and cervical nodes, splenomegaly, elevated LDH, and smoking history is highly suggestive of this diagnosis. We will proceed with an excisional lymph node biopsy to confirm the subtype.
